description: Frozen snapshot of Dataset A (primary_it) — the complete Tranco top-1M .it pool, three combined crawl runs. Separates 'tool version' (crawler/analyzer code, still evolving) from 'dataset version' (this frozen artifact) from 'analysis version' (statistics run against this manifest's data). Not a git tag by design — a dataset snapshot and a tool release are different kinds of artifact with different lifecycles.

runs.note: Predates the measurement_profile system and the DNS/email, well-known, and CORS analyzers (M3). Not retroactively backfilled — this run represents exactly what was measured at the time, no reconstruction.

collection_window.note: Single-day snapshot study, not longitudinal (yet). All three runs collected within the same day.

analysis_subsets.note: Defined so no statistic is silently computed against a base rate it doesn't actually have. 'Full primary_it' is for sample description and coverage reporting, not implicitly assumed as the N for every test.

dataset_A_security_headers_corpus.definition: Every scan with a complete security_headers row (HSTS/CSP/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options/Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy) plus cookies, TLS, fingerprint — covered by all three runs.
dataset_A_security_headers_corpus.coverage: 100% of successful scans across all three runs

dataset_B_extended_security_posture.definition: Successful scans from pilot_5000 + final_remaining_pool only, which have SPF/DMARC/DKIM, security.txt/robots.txt/sitemap.xml, and CORS policy characteristics. Excludes pilot_500 (predates these analyzers).

dataset_C_full_primary_it.definition: All registered sites, regardless of scan outcome — used for sample description, coverage/error-rate reporting, and methodology, not assumed as the base n for every feature-specific test.

known_gaps: 2 domains lost to unhandled per-scan errors (0.02% of the pool), logged in crawl_events, root cause not fully confirmed for either — see paper/data_quality_report.md §6.
scan_metrics missing for pilot_500's 500 scans — table added after that run, not backfilled.
dns_email_security/wellknown_resources/cors_analysis missing for pilot_500's scans — those analyzers (M3) postdate that run, not backfilled — see analysis_subsets above.

anonymization.note: Without a salt, a dictionary attack against known .it domains can invert the hash — domains are public information, so this isn't a severe exposure, but it is not cryptographically irreversible in the way 'anonymized' implies. Use 'pseudonymized domain identifiers' in the paper, not 'anonymized domains'.

anonymized_export.description: One row per scan. Domain replaced with SHA-256(domain) — no cleartext domain, no site_id-to-domain mapping included. Every measured feature flattened: headers, CSP, cookie aggregates, TLS/certificate, DNS/email, well-known, CORS, detected CMS/CDN.

public_export.note: sector and sector_confidence columns are suppressed in the public export (present only in the private working database). Rationale: sector categories University (n=51) and Media (n=28) are derived from small, hand-built, closed candidate lists (~55 and ~34 named entities respectively), and PA (n=156) from an enumerable comune./provincia./regione./.gov.it pattern matching the public ISTAT municipality list. Publishing sector alongside the unsalted domain_sha256 would let an attacker narrow a dictionary attack from the full .it domain space to these small closed lists, meaningfully increasing practical re-identification risk for specific institutions. Aggregate sector counts are still reported in paper/sector_classification.md and the paper itself (Section 4.8); only the per-row public linkage is suppressed.
